input.model_so_far: Main shaft carries gear-gray-L and gear-tan-M (locked); gear-red-P free on its own stub between them.

new_parts.name: sleeve-wht-Q
new_parts.position: locked onto axle-N, sitting inside fork-J's shift slot

new_parts.name: sleeve-blk-S
new_parts.position: locked onto axle-N next to sleeve-wht-Q, forming one combined sliding sleeve

what_each_new_part_touches: sleeve-wht-Q's cross hole locks onto axle-N
sleeve-blk-S's cross hole locks onto axle-N, next to sleeve-wht-Q
where_everything_is_after: sleeve-wht-Q, sleeve-blk-S: new, locked to the main shaft between gear-gray-L and gear-red-P, sitting inside fork-J's slot

why.problem_solved: Adds the sliding dog-clutch collar that fork-J (step 6) will push back and forth to choose a gear.
why.why_these_parts: A cross-hole connector locked to the shaft always turns with it (unlike gear-red-P's free hole), but can still slide along the shaft's length -- that sliding motion, guided by fork-J's slot, is what engages or disengages gear-red-P's clutch face.
why.sets_up_for_later: Sliding this collar toward gear-red-P locks that gear to the shaft for one output speed; sliding it the other way disengages it. Exactly what the other position connects to is not confirmed -- see systems.json.

review_note: Not in catalog/mechanisms.json as a named type -- written here as 'sliding_dog_clutch', a part locked to a shaft (so it always turns with it) but free to slide along the shaft's length inside a fork's slot, engaging a neighboring free gear's clutch face when pushed against it. The exact two shaft positions fork-J selects between, and what the second position (away from gear-red-P) actually engages, isn't shown clearly enough in the booklet to confirm -- flagged in sets/MOC-183729/systems.json open_questions.
